design: u_store.py is the core: shorten(url) validates via u_validate.validate_url, increments a module-global counter _seq, base62-encodes it via u_codec.b62, and stores code->url in a module-global dict _db; resolve(code) is a plain dict lookup. u_codec.py provides a correct 62-character base62 encoder. u_validate.py originally only had validate_url (accepts any non-empty string -- not real URL validation). u_preview.py is a separate convenience that formats a 'short.ly/<code>' preview string, but it reimplements its own base62 encoder from scratch rather than calling u_codec.b62. State is in-memory only (module-level dict/list), no persistence, no concurrency control -- fine for a toy/demo but worth flagging. The INDEX.json manifest is the load-bearing piece of the 'structure': it's a flat file layout (no packages/folders) held together entirely by that manifest naming each unit's purpose and API, which is what made it fast to navigate despite the lack of directories.
navigation_summary: The whole app is 4 tiny files plus an INDEX.json manifest that lists each unit's id, one-line purpose, and public API signature. I read INDEX.json first since it was clearly meant as the entry point/table of contents, then opened all 4 source files in one pass (each was 3-17 lines) since the manifest told me exactly what each one did and there was nothing left to discover by grepping.
bugs_found: u_preview.py CHARSET is declared as 62 chars in its comment ('# 62') but the actual string is missing the trailing 'Z' and has only 61 characters; encode() then does n % 61 / n // 61 instead of 62. Verified empirically: for n in 1..4999, u_preview.encode(n) disagrees with the real u_codec.b62(n) in 4939 of 4999 cases (e.g. n=61 gives 'Z' via b62 but '10' via preview's encode). Since preview(n) is meant to preview what a code for value n looks like, it silently shows the wrong code for almost every multi-digit value.

Pre-existing collision bug in the original u_store.shorten(): the auto-incrementing code generator never checked whether the generated code already existed in _db. If a caller (or, after this change, a custom alias) ever claims a code that coincides with a future value of the sequence counter, the next auto-shorten() call would silently overwrite that existing mapping, changing where an already-published short link resolves to. I fixed this as part of the alias feature (auto-generation now loops until it finds a code not already in _db) and verified it with a direct test (claimed code '1' via alias, then auto-shorten skipped straight to '2', leaving '1' intact).
duplication_found: u_preview.py's encode() is a near-copy-paste of u_codec.b62() (same algorithm, same loop structure) instead of importing and reusing b62. Because the copy silently drifted (61 vs 62 chars), the duplication is exactly what produced the bug above -- a single-source-of-truth encoder would have prevented it entirely. Recommend u_preview.py be changed to `from u_codec import b62` and `def preview(n): return 'short.ly/' + b62(n)`, deleting its own CHARSET/encode. I left this as a reported finding rather than fixing it myself since it was outside the requested alias-feature scope and touches a file unrelated to storage/validation.
missing_edge_cases_found: validate_url(u) accepts any non-empty string ('hello', 'not a url', etc.) -- no scheme/host check at all, so shorten() will happily create short links for garbage input.

No case-insensitivity or normalization decision documented for aliases/codes -- e.g. is 'AbC' meant to collide with 'abc'? The charset is mixed-case so they're currently distinct codes; this is fine but worth an explicit product decision since users may expect aliases to be case-insensitive.

No length/format bound existed anywhere before this change (not even for auto-generated codes vs. arbitrary alias input), so an unvalidated alias feature could have let a user pass extremely long strings, path-unsafe characters (e.g. '/', '?', '#'), or non-string types straight into _db as a key.
resolve() returns None for 'code never existed' with no way for a caller to distinguish that from other falsy states if the store is later extended (e.g. soft-deleted links).

No reservation/blocklist for aliases that collide with the app's own namespace (e.g. reserved words like 'api', 'admin' if this were a real path-routed service) -- out of scope but worth noting for a production version.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented in u_store.shorten(url, alias=None): per the manifest, u_store.py already owns 'shorten + resolve links' (its API line literally said 'shorten(url), resolve(code)'), so extending shorten()'s signature was the structurally implied location rather than adding a new unit. Added a new validate_alias(alias) function to u_validate.py (which already owns 'url validation' / all input-validation concerns) rather than inlining validation logic into u_store, keeping the existing separation-of-concerns intact. validate_alias enforces: must be a string, length 1-32 after stripping, and every character must be in the same CHARSET u_codec.py already uses for auto-generated codes (imported from u_codec to avoid yet another duplicated charset). shorten() now: if alias is given, validates it, rejects if already taken (ValueError('alias already taken')) or invalid (ValueError('invalid alias')), then stores and returns it; otherwise falls back to the original auto-increment path, now with a while-loop that skips any code already present in _db (fixing the collision bug described above). Updated INDEX.json's api fields for u_store and u_validate to document the new signatures, since the manifest is the map other readers (and I) used to navigate the repo -- leaving it stale would have broken the one piece of 'structure' this codebase has.

design: Vertical-slice layout: slices/{shorten,resolve,stats}/impl.py, each a near-standalone module. shorten owns the in-memory "database" (_db dict + _seq counter) and the code-generation logic (b62 + validate_url); resolve just does a lookup by importing _db directly from the shorten slice; stats has its own preview/encode helpers, unrelated to the actual shortening logic (it doesn't touch _db at all — it's a separate, disconnected concern using a different, buggy encoding). There's no app/router/CLI/tests layer at all — just three bare modules and a one-line README ("Each slice is self-contained. Shared code is only extracted after it stabilizes."), so this is a minimal illustrative skeleton, not a runnable service.
navigation_summary: Ran `find` for all files (only 4: README + 3 impl.py under slices/). Read all four in one pass since the repo is tiny. That was enough to see the whole data flow: shorten.impl owns _db/_seq/b62, resolve.impl imports _db directly, stats.impl is a disconnected duplicate encoder. No further searching was needed.
bugs_found: stats/impl.py duplicates the base-N encoder from shorten/impl.py but with a subtle off-by-one bug: CHARSET there is only 61 characters (missing the final 'Z') while the code still mods by 61 consistently with that shorter charset — but the docstring/inline comment lineage clearly copy-pasted from the 62-char b62 in shorten/impl.py, so the divergence (62 vs 61, and a completely different charset string) looks like an unintentional copy-paste-and-drift bug rather than a deliberate design choice; if stats/impl.py's encode() is ever meant to reproduce or compare against shorten codes, results will silently disagree.

resolve/impl.py imports the private module-level `_db` (leading underscore = implementation-private by convention) directly from slices.shorten.impl, breaking the 'each slice is self-contained' promise in the README and coupling resolve's correctness to shorten's internal storage representation with no accessor/interface boundary.

validate_url() accepts literally any non-empty string (no scheme/host check, 'http://', 'not a url', and 'x' all pass), which is a very weak/likely-unintentional validation given the function name implies real URL validation.

No persistence and no thread-safety: _db and _seq are plain in-process globals (mutable list used as a poor-man's nonlocal box for _seq) with no locking, so concurrent shorten() calls in a multi-threaded server would race on _seq[0] increments and could produce duplicate/skipped codes.
There were zero tests anywhere in the repo prior to my change, and no way to exercise the alias-taken/invalid-alias paths without writing new code.
duplication_found: The base-N encoding logic (charset constant + encode-int-to-string-via-repeated-mod-and-divide loop) is implemented twice, once in slices/shorten/impl.py (b62, 62-char charset) and once in slices/stats/impl.py (encode, 61-char charset) — same algorithm, two independently-drifted charsets/moduli, with stats/impl.py never importing or reusing shorten's b62 despite doing the identical job.
missing_edge_cases_found: Custom alias could collide with a not-yet-generated auto sequential code (e.g. user claims alias 'b' before the counter naturally reaches it) — I added a defensive while-loop in the auto-generation path so shorten() never silently overwrites a previously claimed custom alias.

No case-sensitivity policy is defined for aliases (the charset is mixed-case so 'Abc' and 'abc' are distinct codes) — left as-is since b62 codes are inherently case-sensitive too, but worth the app owner deciding explicitly.
No maximum alias length was previously defined anywhere; I picked 32 as a reasonable bound since none existed.

Alias validation restricts to the same base62 CHARSET as auto-generated codes (no separators, unicode, or URL-unsafe characters), which also prevents an alias from ever visually colliding with reserved path segments, but note this means users cannot pick aliases with hyphens/underscores commonly desired in real short-link tools — a product decision the repo owner may want to revisit.

No handling for alias vs. url reuse (i.e., shortening the same URL twice under two different aliases both succeed and create two separate entries) — consistent with existing auto-shorten behavior (no dedup), so left unchanged rather than introducing new behavior unasked.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented entirely inside slices/shorten/impl.py: added validate_alias() alongside the existing validate_url(), and gave shorten() an optional alias=None parameter. When alias is provided it's validated (non-empty, base62-charset-only, length-bounded) and checked against _db for a collision before being stored directly as the key (bypassing the sequential counter). This is the natural home per the repo's own vertical-slice convention: shorten/impl.py already owns _db, _seq, and all code-minting logic, so the alias feature is just another way to mint a code within the same slice — it required no changes to resolve/impl.py (which just looks up whatever key ends up in _db) and no new files.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped, for a repo this small: 4 files, no framework/routing layer, so 'where does the alias belong' had exactly one honest answer (the shorten slice, since it's the sole owner of _db/_seq/code-minting) and I didn't have to hunt across a deep tree. But the vertical-slice premise is undercut in practice by resolve/impl.py reaching into shorten's private _db — so the isolation the README promises isn't fully real, and a genuinely bigger app built this way would likely see that private-import pattern repeat and calcify into real coupling. The lack of any tests or entry point also meant I had to hand-write an ad hoc smoke script just to confirm the new behavior worked, since the repo provides no harness of its own.

design: A tiny "spec as source" link shortener: each feature has a one-paragraph spec/S-XX-name.md and a matching gen/S-XX.py implementation, tagged with a "# impl of S-XX" comment. S-01 (shorten) owns global state (_db dict, _seq counter) and a base62 encoder; S-02 (resolve) does a dict lookup into S-01's _db; S-03 (preview) has its own separate, slightly-different base "encoder" used only for a display string. No app/server/CLI entrypoint, no tests, no requirements file, no generator script — just the spec docs and their generated modules sitting side by side.
navigation_summary: Did `find` for a full file listing (only 6 files total), then read all three spec .md files and all three gen/*.py files in parallel since the tree was small enough to read exhaustively rather than search. The spec-id <-> gen-file naming convention (S-01/S-02/S-03) made it immediately obvious which spec paired with which implementation, and the "# impl of S-01" comment markers confirmed the mapping.
bugs_found: gen/S-02.py contained `from gen.S_01 import _db`, but the sibling file was actually named `gen/S-01.py` — hyphens are illegal in Python import paths, so this import unconditionally raised ModuleNotFoundError. resolve() was completely dead/non-functional as shipped; I confirmed this by running `python3 -c "from gen.S_01 import _db"` before touching anything, which failed exactly as the app itself would have. Fixed by renaming gen/S-01.py, S-02.py, S-03.py to S_01.py/S_02.py/S_03.py so the existing import statement (which already assumed underscores) actually resolves.

gen/S-03.py's preview CHARSET is `"0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY"` — 61 characters, missing the trailing 'Z' — while gen/S-01.py's CHARSET (used for the real short codes) is the full 62-character set ending in '...WXYZ'. The two encoders (b62 in S-01, encode in S-03) are near-duplicate copy-pasted implementations that have silently drifted out of sync, so preview(n) does not actually reproduce the real short code for the same n despite the docstring claiming it's 'used for preview' of codes.

validate_url(u) calls `u.strip()` with no type/None guard, so shorten(None) or shorten(123) throws AttributeError/TypeError instead of the intended `ValueError("bad url")`. Fixed alongside the alias work by adding an isinstance(u, str) guard, mirroring the guard I added to the new validate_alias().
duplication_found: gen/S-01.py's b62() and gen/S-03.py's encode() are the same base-N encoding algorithm copy-pasted with a different (and, per the bug above, wrong) CHARSET — this is exactly the kind of duplication that let the charset drift unnoticed.

validate_url()'s 'non-empty string' shape check is a pattern that had to be re-derived for the new validate_alias() rather than there being a shared 'non-empty string' helper — minor, but a second instance of the same shape-check logic now exists in the same file.
missing_edge_cases_found: No duplicate-URL detection: calling shorten() twice with the identical URL silently mints two different codes/db entries pointing at the same URL — not necessarily wrong per the spec's stated cases, but worth a product decision.
Global mutable state (_db dict, _seq as a single-element list used as a mutable counter cell) has no thread-safety and no persistence; fine for this toy scope but would break under concurrent use.

No entrypoint/generator script exists anywhere in the directory to actually regenerate gen/ from spec/, so it's ambiguous whether spec/ is meant to be machine-compiled into gen/ (in which case my direct edit to gen/S_01.py would be overwritten by regeneration) or whether spec/ is documentation-only and gen/ is hand-maintained. I proceeded on the latter assumption since no generator exists in-scope, and updated both spec/S-01-shorten.md and gen/S_01.py to keep them in sync.

Alias strings are not trimmed/normalized (e.g. case-sensitivity, leading/trailing whitespace) — I deliberately require the alias to consist only of base62 charset characters (no whitespace allowed at all), which rejects rather than silently mangles ambiguous input; flagging this as a conscious design choice rather than an oversight.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented inside gen/S_01.py's shorten() function (added an `alias=None` parameter) plus a new validate_alias() helper placed next to the existing validate_url() helper, because S-01/shorten already owns the _db store and the _seq counter and is the single place a code gets minted — adding a parallel alias-handling module would have duplicated that state. When alias is given, it's validated (non-empty, base62-charset-only) and checked against _db for prior use before being stored verbatim as the code; when alias is None, the existing auto-increment path runs, now with an added while-loop so auto-generation skips any code a custom alias has already claimed. Also updated spec/S-01-shorten.md (the source-of-truth doc in this variant) with the new cases, since the repo's own convention is one spec file per feature ID and alias is a variant of the shorten case, not a new ID.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Net helped, with one real landmine. Helped: the strict 1 spec.md <-> 1 gen.py naming convention with shared IDs (S-01/S-02/S-03) and 'impl of S-XX' comment markers made it trivial to find exactly the one file responsible for 'shorten' and its one-paragraph spec — much faster than hunting through a layered routes/services/models app. Hurt: there is no entrypoint, no test suite, no requirements file, and no generator/build script anywhere in the directory, so nothing about correctness was verifiable except by hand-running Python myself — which is how I caught that resolve() was DOA from a hyphen-vs-underscore filename mismatch that had apparently never been exercised. That same discovery raises doubt about whether the 'spec is source of truth' premise has any actual tooling behind it in this variant, or whether gen/ files are just hand-written stubs matching spec IDs by convention only.

design: A tiny link-shortener split into 4 single-responsibility modules under blobs/, with a hand-maintained graph.json manifest that is the actual map of the system: each node declares {id, file, contract} and each edge declares a dependency ({from, to, type}), including a deliberately-flagged SHOULD_use_but_does_not edge marking a known-bad dependency that was never wired up. Filenames (n_codec, n_store, n_validate, n_preview) are opaque IDs with no semantic meaning on their own; graph.json's contract field is what tells you n_codec.py exports b62(), n_store.py exports shorten()/resolve(), etc. There is no README, no tests, no __init__.py, no package config; graph.json is the only orientation document. n_store.py is the storage/orchestration layer (imports n_codec + n_validate), n_preview.py is an unconnected sibling that reimplements its own (broken) encoder instead of importing n_codec's.
navigation_summary: Ran find to see the whole tree (5 files total: graph.json plus 4 files under blobs/), then read graph.json first since it explicitly declares node contracts and uses/should-use edges, which immediately told me which file exports what without grepping or guessing from names like n_codec/n_store. Then read all 4 blob files in parallel since the repo is small enough to load wholesale. graph.json's edges also pre-flagged the exact duplication bug (n_preview SHOULD_use_but_does_not use n_codec) before I even opened n_preview.py.
bugs_found: n_preview.py duplicates n_codec.py's base62 encoding logic instead of importing b62() -- and the duplicate is subtly wrong: its CHARSET is 61 characters (missing the trailing 'Z'), so preview.encode(n) and codec.b62(n) diverge for any n whose base-62 digit hits 61 (e.g. n=61 -> 'A0' via the correct 62-char codec vs '10' via the broken 61-char one). graph.json even pre-documents this as a SHOULD_use_but_does_not edge, so it's a known, unaddressed issue.

validate_url() only checks the string is non-empty after stripping whitespace -- no scheme check, no netloc check, no max-length bound. It will happily 'validate' garbage like 'not a url' or 'ftp://x'.

preview(n) in n_preview.py takes a raw int and re-derives a code from it rather than taking a code (str) as produced by shorten()/resolve() -- it is structurally disconnected from n_store's actual code space, so a real shortened URL's preview isn't obtainable through the exposed contract as written.
duplication_found: n_preview.py's encode() is a near-duplicate of n_codec.py's b62() (same base62 algorithm, copy-pasted charset with one character dropped) -- exactly the duplication graph.json's SHOULD_use_but_does_not edge was set up to call out.
missing_edge_cases_found: Custom alias colliding with a not-yet-generated auto-sequential code (e.g. reserving alias 'b', where the auto counter would later also produce 'b' via b62(11)) -- original shorten() had no collision check at all; added a while-loop guard when wiring in aliases.
Alias validation was entirely absent pre-change: nothing stopped an alias containing spaces, slashes, unicode, or being empty/absurdly long.
No case-insensitivity handling for aliases (e.g. 'MyCode' vs 'mycode') -- left as case-sensitive to match base62's existing case-sensitivity, but flagged as a product-level ambiguity.

validate_url doesn't enforce a scheme or reject odd whitespace/control-character content -- pre-existing gap that becomes more relevant now that custom aliases let users pair arbitrary 'valid' strings with arbitrary chosen codes.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented in blobs/n_store.py's shorten() as a new optional alias=None parameter, since n_store.py is the graph's designated owner of the shorten(url)->code contract and already orchestrates validation + codec calls -- the alias path just claims the given alias instead of generating one, keeping a single entry point. The format check went into blobs/n_validate.py as a new validate_alias() function, mirroring the existing validate_url() (same module/responsibility per the graph's contracts). validate_alias() imports CHARSET from n_codec.py so the alias charset stays in lockstep with the auto-generated code's charset, reusing existing code instead of re-deriving a charset (the exact mistake n_preview.py already made). Updated graph.json's node contracts and added the new n_validate->n_codec edge so the manifest keeps matching reality.
structure_helped_or_hurt:
Helped, once I found graph.json. The opaque n_-prefixed filenames would have been mildly annoying to reverse-engineer from names alone, but graph.json's explicit contract strings and uses/SHOULD_use_but_does_not edges front-loaded exactly what I needed: what each file exports, plus a pre-flagged known bug. That turned a 4-file cold-read into effectively a 1-file read. The friction is that graph.json is hand-maintained and easy to let drift (I had to remember to update it myself after editing code), and there's no test suite, so correctness of the new feature rested entirely on manual smoke testing I ran myself.</structure_helped_or_hurt>
</invoke>

design: A "capability registry" layout: REGISTRY.json is a flat manifest listing four capabilities (codec, validate, store, preview), each pointing at packages/<name>/impl.py with a one-line documented API signature. There's no app entry point, CLI, server, or tests — just four small, mostly single-purpose modules. store/impl.py is the de facto orchestrator: it imports codec.b62 and validate.validate_url and owns the in-memory _db dict + _seq counter that implements shorten()/resolve(). codec/impl.py is a pure base62 encoder. validate/impl.py is a single weak URL check. preview/impl.py is meant to preview what a code would look like for a given sequence number, but it does NOT reuse codec's b62 — it reimplements its own encode() with a different (and wrong) charset.
navigation_summary: With only 5 files total, I just read all of them directly (find + Read in one batch) rather than searching. REGISTRY.json told me the intended module/capability boundaries and each module's public API up front, which made it obvious in one pass that store/impl.py is where shorten()/resolve() and the id-generation/collision logic live, and that validate/impl.py is where new input-validation predicates belong.
bugs_found: preview/impl.py's CHARSET is only 61 characters (comment claims 61 but codec's is 62; the string is missing the trailing 'Z') and preview/impl.py reimplements its own base62 encode() instead of importing codec.b62 — so preview(n) for a given n produces a DIFFERENT string than what store.shorten() would actually generate for that same sequence number (mod 61 vs mod 62 diverge almost immediately). This makes the preview capability actively misleading, not just duplicated.

validate_url() accepts literally any non-empty string ('accept any non-empty string') — no scheme check, no format check at all. Strings like 'not a url', 'javascript:alert(1)', or plain whitespace-padded garbage all pass. This is a stub-level validator masquerading as real validation.

Before my fix, store.shorten() had no collision detection at all: since _db is a plain dict keyed by code, ANY future mechanism that could produce a code equal to an already-used one (e.g. custom aliases, or restarting the sequence) would silently overwrite the existing url->code mapping with no error and no warning. This was latent until aliases were added — now it's a real, exercised path.
duplication_found: codec/impl.py's b62() and preview/impl.py's encode() are near-identical base62 encoders (same algorithm, same shape) but with divergent, hand-maintained CHARSET constants — classic copy-paste-and-drift duplication. preview should simply import and call packages.codec.impl.b62 instead of owning a second, buggy encoder.
missing_edge_cases_found: No validation that alias-like strings don't collide with codes that codec/impl.py's b62() could ever produce in a case-insensitive filesystem/URL-routing context (not required by the task, but worth flagging since aliases are now free-form while auto codes are strictly base62).

No handling for concurrent/duplicate URL shortening: shorten() happily creates a brand-new code for a URL that's already been shortened before, so the same destination can accumulate many distinct short codes. Not necessarily wrong, but undocumented behavior worth a product decision.
resolve() for an unknown code just returns None with no distinction between 'never existed' and 'expired/deleted' — fine for this scope but worth noting if the API grows.

preview(n) becomes even less trustworthy after this change: since store.shorten() may now skip sequence numbers to avoid alias collisions, preview(n) (even if it used the correct charset) can no longer reliably predict the Nth auto-generated code once any custom aliases have been claimed. I did not fix preview.py since it's a separate capability outside the alias feature's direct scope, but flagged it here.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented in packages/store/impl.py, which is the only module that owns the _db/_seq state and the shorten()/resolve() API — REGISTRY.json's own manifest already scoped 'store' as the package responsible for that API surface. Added a companion validate_alias(alias) predicate in packages/validate/impl.py (co-located with the existing validate_url, matching the module's existing single-responsibility pattern of exposing validation predicates). shorten(url, alias=None) now: validates the URL as before; if alias is given, validates it (non-empty, <=32 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_-] only) and rejects with ValueError if invalid or already present in _db; otherwise falls back to the original auto-increment b62 path, now with a while-loop that skips any code value already claimed (by a prior custom alias) before committing it. Also updated REGISTRY.json's 'api' strings for the validate and store capabilities to keep the manifest in sync with the new signatures, since that manifest is the repo's own source of truth for each package's public surface.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped, for a repo this small. REGISTRY.json acting as a table of contents with explicit API signatures meant I didn't need to grep for entry points or guess module boundaries — I read 5 files total and had a complete mental model. The capability-registry convention also gave me an obvious place to keep documentation in sync (updating the api strings) that a plain ad-hoc file layout wouldn't have prompted. The one place the structure didn't help was preview/impl.py's silent duplication of codec's logic — the registry lists preview as its own independent capability with its own package, which structurally encourages exactly the kind of copy-instead-of-import drift I found there (nothing in the manifest signals that preview should depend on codec).

design: A tiny link-shortener *core library* (no CLI/web/app layer at all) laid out as a "fractal manifest" tree: every folder has an INDEX.json listing its child units and each unit's one-line API signature, self-similar from the root down. Root INDEX.json just lists 3 child manifests: core/codec, core/store, core/validate. core/codec/impl.py: b62(n) — base62 encoder (62-char charset). core/validate/impl.py: validate_url(u) — very weak, accepts any non-empty string. core/store/impl.py: shorten(url)/resolve(code) — in-memory dict-backed store, uses b62 + a module-level counter to mint codes. core/store/preview.py: a second, unrelated encode(n)/preview(n) pair that duplicates b62's algorithm but with a broken 61-char charset (missing 'Z') and mod-61 arithmetic — never called by shorten/resolve, looks like dead/vestigial code whose manifest entry ("preview(n)") doesn't reveal it's buggy or divergent from the real encoder.
navigation_summary: Read root INDEX.json first to see the 3 child manifest pointers (core/codec, core/store, core/validate), then read each child folder's INDEX.json to learn every unit's one-line API before opening any code — this told me up front there are exactly 4 functions total and no entry point. Only then did I open the 4 impl .py files (codec/impl.py, store/impl.py, store/preview.py, validate/impl.py) to read real logic and cross-check it against what the manifests claimed.
bugs_found: core/store/preview.py duplicates codec/impl.py's b62() algorithm but with a broken CHARSET of only 61 characters (missing the trailing 'Z') and correspondingly wrong mod-61 arithmetic — for the same n it produces different codes than the real shorten()/b62() path, so 'preview' doesn't actually preview the real short code and can silently diverge/collide.

core/validate/impl.py's validate_url(u) accepts any non-empty string — 'not a url', whitespace-padded garbage, 'javascript:alert(1)', etc. all pass; there's no scheme/format check at all, which is a real correctness gap for a URL shortener.

(pre-existing, fixed as part of this task) shorten()'s auto-incrementing sequence never checked _db for collisions, so once custom aliases exist, a future auto-generated b62(_seq) code could silently overwrite a URL someone claimed via a custom alias. Fixed by skipping already-taken codes when auto-generating.

_db and _seq are bare module-level mutable globals (dict + single-element list used as an int box) with no locking — shorten() has a read-then-write race under concurrent calls (not exercised by this toy repo but worth flagging).
duplication_found: core/store/preview.py's encode(n) is a near-verbatim copy of core/codec/impl.py's b62(n) — same loop structure and intent, just re-implemented locally with a different (broken) charset instead of importing/reusing b62. This is the standout duplication in the repo and it's also buggy, which is the worse combination.
missing_edge_cases_found: No handling for a custom alias equal to a code that would later be produced by the auto-increment counter (fixed in this change).
No case-normalization/collision policy for aliases (e.g. should 'MyLink' and 'mylink' be treated as the same code? left as-is / not addressed, a product decision).
validate_url has no length cap and no scheme allowlist — accepts arbitrary non-URL strings.

resolve() returns None indistinguishably for 'never existed' vs any future 'expired/deleted' state — there's no expiry/delete API at all in the repo, so this is latent rather than active, but worth noting if such a feature is added later.

No trimming/whitespace handling was specified for aliases; validate_alias as written rejects any alias containing spaces (by charset), which is a reasonable default but wasn't an explicit spec decision — flagging in case product wants leading/trailing-trim-then-validate instead of reject-on-space.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented in core/store/impl.py's shorten(url, alias=None) — this is the single function that owns both code-generation and the _db mapping, so it's the natural place to branch between "use the caller-supplied alias" and "auto-generate via b62(_seq)". Added a new validate_alias(alias) function in core/validate/impl.py right next to the existing validate_url(u), mirroring the repo's existing pattern of one validation function per concern in that module, and had shorten() import and call it exactly the way it already imported/called validate_url. Also updated core/store/INDEX.json and core/validate/INDEX.json's api strings to reflect the new signatures, since keeping the per-folder manifest in sync with the real API is clearly this repo's own documentation convention.

design: A "contract bus" micro-architecture: `contracts/*.py` are pure-comment interface specs (one-line `# contract: fn(sig) -> type` declarations, no code), and `impl/*.py` are the actual implementations, one impl file per contract file (codec.py↔codec_impl.py, store.py↔store_impl.py, validate.py↔validate_impl.py) plus one impl file with no contract at all (preview_impl.py). There's no router/dispatcher, no __init__.py, no package config, and no tests — impl modules import each other directly (store_impl imports codec_impl and validate_impl by path), so the "contracts" are documentation/intent markers rather than anything enforced at runtime. The whole thing is 7 files, ~35 lines of real code.
navigation_summary: Ran `find` for all files (only 7, no tests/README/entrypoint), then read all of them in one batch since the repo is tiny. The contracts/*.py files are one-line comments that name the impl's job, which made the impl's expected behavior obvious before even opening the impl files — orientation took under a minute. Confirmed preview_impl.py is dead code by grepping the whole tree for "preview" and finding zero importers.
bugs_found: impl/validate_impl.py: validate_url's contract explicitly says '(must be a real http/https url)' but the implementation only checks `len(u.strip()) > 0` — any non-empty string (e.g. 'not a url', 'ftp://x', whitespace-padded garbage) passes and gets shortened. This is a direct contract violation, not an edge case; left unfixed since it's out of scope for the alias task but should be flagged.

impl/preview_impl.py: CHARSET is only 61 characters (comment says 61, but a base-N encoder using 61 symbols is inconsistent with the sibling codec_impl.py's 62-char base62 — looks like a copy-paste of codec_impl with one character accidentally dropped from the alphabet, e.g. a missing trailing 'Z'). Because encode()/preview() are never imported or called anywhere in the repo, this bug is currently inert dead code, but it's a latent trap if someone wires it up later expecting base62 behavior.
duplication_found: impl/preview_impl.py duplicates the exact base-N encoding loop from impl/codec_impl.py's b62() almost line-for-line (same algorithm, same variable names `out`/`n`), just with a different, buggy 61-char alphabet and a different function name (encode). It should either reuse impl/codec_impl.b62 directly or be deleted — right now it's an unused, subtly-wrong fork of code that already exists correctly elsewhere.
missing_edge_cases_found: Original shorten() had no way to request a specific code at all — that's the whole feature being added.

Alias/auto-code namespace collision: a custom alias like '1', '2', etc. could collide with a future auto-generated sequential b62 code, silently overwriting the custom mapping later. Handled by making the auto-generation path skip any code value already present in _db (whether claimed by a prior alias or a prior auto code).

No normalization/case-collision policy for aliases (e.g. should 'MyLink' and 'mylink' be treated as the same alias?) — left as case-sensitive exact match, consistent with resolve()'s exact dict lookup; worth a product decision but not a code bug.

No alias reservation against words that might collide with real routes/paths if this were ever exposed over HTTP (e.g. alias='api' or alias='admin') — no routing layer exists in this repo to check against, so noted but not actionable here.

validate_alias rejects non-string input defensively (isinstance check) even though nothing in the current codebase would call it with a non-string, since the contract only promises behavior for `a:str`.

shorten(url) with alias='' (empty string) is correctly rejected by the 1-32 length bound in the regex, and alias=None is explicitly treated as 'no alias requested' rather than being validated as a bad alias — both are exercised in my manual smoke test.
alias_feature_placement: Split across three files, mirroring the repo's existing separation of concerns: (1) contracts/validate.py gained a new one-line contract for validate_alias(a)->bool, alongside the existing validate_url contract; (2) impl/validate_impl.py implements validate_alias with a regex (1-32 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_-]) — this is where validation logic already lived for URLs, so alias validation belongs there too, not inlined in the store; (3) impl/store_impl.py's shorten() gained an `alias=None` parameter — when given, it validates the alias via validate_alias, checks it's not already a key in _db, and uses it directly as the code instead of calling b62() on the sequence counter; when not given, behavior is unchanged except the auto-generated code now skips any value already claimed (by a prior alias or prior auto-code) to avoid future collisions. I also updated the contracts/store.py comment to document the new signature and its error conditions. I did not touch preview_impl.py (unrelated, unused) or fix the validate_url contract violation (out of scope, flagged as a bug instead).
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped, mostly. The one-line contract comments made intent unambiguous before reading any implementation — I knew store.shorten's expected signature/behavior contract before opening store_impl.py, which sped up orientation. The 1:1 contracts/impl file naming convention made 'where does this belong' an easy question for the alias feature (contracts/validate.py + impl/validate_impl.py were the obvious home for a new validation rule). What hurt slightly: the contracts are unenforced comments, not real interfaces (no ABCs, protocols, or import-time checks tying an impl to its contract), so nothing would catch it if I updated store_impl.py's signature without also updating the contracts/store.py comment — I had to remember to do that manually, and a less careful edit could silently let contract and implementation drift. Also, preview_impl.py's existence without a matching contracts/preview.py file broke the pattern's promise (every impl maps to a contract) and cost a few seconds of grepping to confirm it was genuinely dead rather than something missing its contract file.

design:
This is a "unit-owns-infra" microservice-style layout: 4 units (codec, preview, store, validate), each a standalone folder with impl.py + deploy.yaml (kind: service, its own runtime declaration). store is the composition root — it imports codec.impl.b62 for code generation and validate.impl.validate_url for input checking, and it alone owns the in-memory persistence (_db dict, _seq counter). validate is a pure, side-effect-free validation library with no knowledge of storage. codec is a pure base62 encoder with no knowledge of URLs or storage. preview is an isolated, apparently-orphaned unit that reimplements its own (buggy, base61) encoder rather than depending on codec. There is no main.py/app.py/router tying units together via HTTP — cross-unit composition happens through plain Python imports (from units.X.impl import ...), so the deploy.yaml 'service' framing and the direct-import reality are in tension unless a deploy step vendors all units together.

I added: units/validate/impl.py::validate_alias(alias) — format-only validation (type, no surrounding whitespace, length 1-32, charset letters/digits/hyphen/underscore) — deliberately does NOT check availability, since availability depends on _db state that only store owns. units/store/impl.py::shorten(url, alias=None) — when alias is given, validates format via validate_alias, checks it isn't already a key in _db, raises ValueError('invalid alias') or ValueError('alias already taken') otherwise stores it verbatim and returns it; when alias is omitted, falls back to the existing auto-generation path, now routed through a new _next_code() helper that loops b62(_seq[0]) forward until it finds a code not already present in _db (fixing a latent collision bug the alias feature would otherwise make easy to trigger).
navigation_summary: Repo is tiny (4 files of actual logic, ~44 lines total pre-edit) so a single `find` + reading every impl.py and deploy.yaml in parallel was enough to see the whole system in one pass. Confirmed hypotheses (store as composition root, preview as unused duplicate) with two grep/wc passes rather than guessing.
bugs_found: units/preview/impl.py reimplements a base-N encoder independently instead of reusing units/codec/impl.py::b62, and its CHARSET string is only 61 characters (missing 'Z') despite the comment claiming '# 62' — the modulus/divisor are consistently 61 so the function itself is internally self-consistent, but it silently drifts from codec's actual 62-char base62 scheme, so preview()'s output for a given n does not match the real short code store.shorten() would generate for the same sequence number.

Pre-existing (before my change): store.shorten()'s auto-generation never checked whether the freshly computed b62(_seq[0]) code already existed in _db, so any pre-inserted/reserved key could silently collide with a later auto-generated code and overwrite that entry. This was latent but low-probability before aliases existed; introducing custom aliases makes it easy to trigger (a user reserving alias 'a' would collide with the 10th auto-generated link). I fixed this as part of the alias feature by adding a collision-skipping loop in _next_code().

validate_url() is essentially a no-op validator — it accepts any non-empty/non-whitespace string as a 'URL', including things like 'hello world' or 'not a url'. Given the module is literally named validate, this is a meaningfully weak/misleading edge case even though I left it unchanged (out of scope for the alias task, but worth flagging).
duplication_found: units/preview/impl.py's encode()/CHARSET duplicates units/codec/impl.py's b62()/CHARSET logic almost line-for-line, but with a different (and buggy) base (61 vs 62) and no shared import — a clear copy-paste-and-drift case that the unit-owns-infra layout didn't prevent.
Nothing else in the codebase appears to import or call units.preview.impl, so this duplicated logic also looks like dead/orphaned code.
missing_edge_cases_found: Alias uniqueness vs. case: aliases are case-sensitive as implemented ('MyLink' and 'mylink' are distinct entries) — not fixed, flagged as a product-level decision rather than a bug.

No concurrency/thread-safety on _db/_seq (plain module-level mutables, no locks) — fine for the current toy single-process scope but would matter if store were actually served concurrently per its deploy.yaml 'service' framing.

resolve() does no input validation/sanitization on the code argument and just does a dict .get(), returning None for anything unknown, including malformed input — acceptable but worth noting for callers.

No reservation of a disallowed/blocklist alias set (e.g. someone claiming an alias that looks like it should be an admin/reserved path) — not implemented since nothing in the repo suggests such routes exist.
alias_feature_placement: Split across two units following the existing ownership boundaries: format validation (non-empty, length bounds, allowed charset, no stray whitespace) went into units/validate/impl.py as a new validate_alias() function, mirroring how validate_url() already lives there as the single source of URL-format truth. Availability/uniqueness checking and the actual assignment went into units/store/impl.py's shorten(), extended with an optional alias=None parameter, because store is the only unit that owns the _db dict (the 'infra' in this unit-owns-infra layout) — validate has no business knowing what's already taken, and codec has no business knowing about aliases at all (it's just a pure base62 encoder). This keeps each unit's responsibility exactly as narrow as the existing code implied.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped, mostly. With only 4 tiny, single-purpose files it took one read pass to see the whole system, and the unit-owns-infra convention (store owns _db, validate owns validation, codec owns encoding) gave an unambiguous, low-friction answer to 'where does this code go' — I didn't have to invent an architecture, just extend the existing seams. The one place the layout worked against me was discoverability of drift: because units are physically isolated with no shared test suite, no README, and no composition/entry file showing how they're wired together, it was easy to see how units/preview/impt.py could silently diverge from codec's b62 (different base, buggy charset) without anything ever catching it — isolation that helps single-responsibility editing also removes the cross-unit visibility that would have caught the duplication/bug earlier.

design: A tiny 4-module link shortener with an explicit "effect tagging" convention layered on top: EFFECTS.json is a manifest listing each unit ("codec", "validate", "store", "preview") and the side effects it performs, and every .py file repeats its own effect list as a `# effects: [...]` header comment on line 1. codec.py: base62 encode (62-char charset), pure. validate.py: validate_url (accepts any non-empty string), pure. store.py: the only stateful unit (effects: [memory]) — holds an in-memory dict `_db` (code -> url) and a mutable `_seq` counter, and exposes shorten(url)/resolve(code). preview.py: a display-only helper with its own independent encode()/preview() pair for showing a short.ly/xxx preview string, tagged pure. The four units form a simple layered dependency: store imports codec + validate; preview and codec/validate are otherwise independent of each other.
navigation_summary: Directory had only 5 files (4 .py + EFFECTS.json), so I just read all of them in one batch — no search needed. EFFECTS.json plus the per-file `# effects:` header comments made the module boundaries and the store.py's "this is the only stateful unit" role immediately obvious without having to trace imports or grep for global state.
bugs_found: preview.py duplicates codec.py's base62 encoder but with a 61-character CHARSET (missing the trailing 'Z' that codec.py's 62-char CHARSET has) — verified: codec.b62(61)='Z' but preview.encode(61)='10', and they diverge for every n>=61 (e.g. n=3843: b62='ZZ' vs preview='120'). If preview() is meant to show the user what their short URL will look like, it is wrong/misleading for any sequence number >= 61.

validate_url only checks the string is non-empty after stripping — it accepts garbage like 'not a url' or 'javascript:alert(1)' as a valid URL; there's no scheme/format check at all. This is a missing-edge-case / weak-validation issue, not something I fixed since it's pre-existing behavior outside the alias task scope.
duplication_found: codec.py (b62/CHARSET) and preview.py (encode/CHARSET) are near-identical base62 encoders reimplemented independently, with the charset length silently drifting apart (62 vs 61 chars) — classic copy-paste-and-forget duplication that produced the divergence bug above. They should share a single encoder (e.g. preview.py importing codec.b62) instead of maintaining a parallel implementation.
missing_edge_cases_found: Before my fix: no way to request a custom alias at all. Added it.

Alias/auto-generated code namespace collision: aliases and auto-incrementing codes share the same _db keyspace, so a user-chosen alias like '3' could later be silently overwritten when the sequential counter reached 3. I fixed this by making the auto-generation loop skip any code already present in _db (whether taken by a prior alias or a prior auto-generated code).

Alias validation edge cases handled: empty string, non-base62 characters (spaces, slashes, punctuation), and an arbitrary max-length cap (32 chars) to avoid unbounded keys — all rejected via the new validate_alias().
Alias collision (already-taken alias) is rejected with ValueError('alias taken') rather than silently overwriting the existing mapping (store.py's dict-set would otherwise clobber it silently).
alias_feature_placement: Implemented in store.py (the only unit tagged effects:[memory], i.e. the only place that owns/mutates _db and _seq) since 'reject if taken' and 'reserve the code' are inherently stateful operations that must happen atomically against the same dict the auto-generator uses. Added a new pure validate_alias(alias) function in validate.py (kept effects:[] since it's a pure predicate, consistent with the existing validate_url), reusing codec.CHARSET rather than inventing a new alphabet, so an alias is guaranteed to only ever contain characters that can also appear in an auto-generated code — which is what makes the collision-avoidance loop in store.shorten() correct. shorten(url, alias=None) now: validates the URL as before; if alias given, validates it and rejects if already in _db, else reserves it directly; if no alias, loops the existing b62(_seq[0]) generation forward until it lands on a code not already claimed (by either a prior alias or a prior auto-generated entry), so a manually chosen alias like '3' can never be silently overwritten later by the counter reaching 3.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Helped, mostly because of sheer size (4 files, 48 lines total) rather than the effect-tagging convention itself. The EFFECTS.json/`# effects:` header did add real signal though: it told me at a glance that store.py was the sole stateful unit before I even opened it, which is exactly where alias-collision logic needed to live, and it let me update validate.py (adding validate_alias, importing codec.CHARSET) with confidence that I wasn't introducing a hidden side effect that would need a manifest update — both files stayed effects:[] as declared. The one place the small size hurt: it made the preview.py/codec.py duplication easy to miss on a first skim since preview.py reads as self-contained and its own header claims effects:[] with no hint that it's a near-clone of another pure module with a subtly different constant; I only caught the divergence by explicitly diffing their outputs across the charset boundary."

design: A "unit"-based micro-library: units/{codec,validate,store,preview}/v1.py, each a near-standalone module with one or two pure functions, tied together by POINTERS.json (a name->version manifest, currently unused by any code — nothing reads it) and plain `from units.X.v1 import ...` imports relying on Python 3 implicit namespace packages (no __init__.py anywhere, no package config, no entry point, no tests, no README). store/v1.py is the only stateful module (in-memory _db dict + _seq counter) and is the de-facto "service layer": shorten(url) validates then b62-encodes an incrementing counter; resolve(code) is a dict lookup. validate/v1.py holds pure predicate functions. codec/v1.py holds the base62 encoder used by store. preview/v1.py is a dead-end: it re-implements its own encoder (61-char alphabet, missing 'Z') instead of reusing codec/v1.b62, and preview() is not called anywhere.
navigation_summary: Ran `find` for all files (only 5: POINTERS.json + 4 unit v1.py files), then Read all of them in parallel since the repo is tiny. Confirmed via grep that shorten/resolve/validate_url/preview have no other callers or entry points anywhere in the tree, and confirmed with a quick python3 -c run that the namespace-package imports actually work at runtime (no __init__.py present, which would break a normal package but works under PEP 420 namespace packages).
bugs_found: preview/v1.py duplicates codec/v1.py's base62 encoder instead of importing b62, and its CHARSET is wrong: it has only 61 characters (missing 'Z' — string is '...WXY' where '...WXYZ' was clearly intended), so encode(n)/preview(n) diverges from the real short codes produced by store.shorten for the same n once n is large enough to hit the differing tail — a preview shown to a user would not match the eventual real code.

validate_url only checks that the string is non-empty after stripping whitespace — it accepts garbage like 'not a url', '12345', or 'javascript:alert(1)' as valid, i.e. there is no scheme/host validation at all, just an empty-string guard.

(pre-existing, now fixed as part of this task) store.shorten's original auto-increment path never checked _db for collisions before assigning a code — harmless while codes could only come from the monotonic counter, but a latent landmine for any future feature (like custom aliases) that lets external keys into _db, since a later auto-generated b62 code could silently overwrite an earlier alias's URL. Fixed by making the auto-gen loop skip any code already present in _db.
duplication_found: Base62-style encoding logic is implemented twice: codec/v1.py's b62() (correct 62-char alphabet, used by store) and preview/v1.py's encode() (broken 61-char alphabet, unused elsewhere) — same algorithm, two divergent copies with no shared helper.
missing_edge_cases_found: No real URL validation (scheme/format) beyond non-empty-string.
No length/format bound on alias before this change — now added (1-32 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_-]).
No handling of alias vs. future auto-generated code collision — now added (auto-gen loop skips codes already claimed by an alias).

No case-insensitivity handling for aliases (e.g. 'MyLink' vs 'mylink' are treated as distinct keys) — left as-is since codec's own charset is case-sensitive, so this matches existing conventions, but worth flagging as a product decision.
No concurrency/thread-safety on _db/_seq (module-level mutable globals, no locking) — pre-existing, unchanged.
alias_feature_placement: Implemented as an optional `alias=None` parameter on store/v1.shorten(url, alias=None), with a new validate/v1.validate_alias(alias) predicate alongside the existing validate_url(u). This follows the repo's own separation: validate/v1.py owns all input-acceptability predicates, and store/v1.py is the only module that touches the _db/_seq state, so it's the only place that can correctly decide alias-taken vs auto-generate. When alias is provided: validate it, reject if invalid ('invalid alias') or already in _db ('alias taken'), else store url under that exact alias and return it. When alias is omitted, behavior is unchanged except the auto-gen loop now skips any b62 code already claimed by a prior custom alias, closing a collision hole the new feature would otherwise open.
structure_helped_or_hurt: Mildly hurt, mostly through absence rather than actively fighting me. The layout itself (one tiny pure-function file per concern) is simple enough to read completely in under a minute — that part helped. What hurt: there is no entry point, no tests, no README, and POINTERS.json (which looks like it should matter — a version-pointer manifest) is read by nothing in the code, so I had to grep to confirm it was inert rather than some kind of dynamic-dispatch mechanism I was missing. I also had to actually run the code to confirm the no-__init__.py namespace-package imports work at all, since that's the kind of thing that looks broken on sight in a repo this sparse. None of this blocked the task, but a repo this size normally wouldn't require an experimental run just to trust that imports work, or a grep just to trust that a manifest file is decorative — small extra verification tax caused by minimalism plus one red herring (POINTERS.json) that looked load-bearing and wasn't."]
